text: Every stage of procure-to-pay is carried out by someone with a specific job, in a work area built for that job. Before we follow LTV Manufacturing's bearing purchase through the system, let's meet the roles and where each one actually logs in.

A requester, like Dana, submits a requisition from Self Service Procurement. A buyer, like Marcus, turns that into a purchase order from the Purchase Orders work area. Receiving personnel, like Priya, confirm the goods arrived. And an AP processor, like Chen, matches and validates the supplier's invoice in Payables.

It helps to separate two ideas. A module, like Purchasing or Payables, is how Oracle organizes functionality behind the scenes. A work area is the landing page a person actually opens, scoped tightly to their job. A requester's screen hides everything a buyer needs, and a buyer's screen hides everything an AP processor needs.

As a consultant, you'll often be asked to diagnose a problem in a role you don't personally hold. If a requisition disappears, it's usually sitting in someone else's approval queue, not lost. Function security and segregation of duties policies are often the real reason a user can't see a button, not a bug.

Each stage has an owner, working inside a work area scoped to their job, protected by security policies you'll learn to recognize rather than configure. Up next, lesson three: reviewing the procurement setup that makes all of this possible - business units and procurement agents.
